_sources.title: Taking a Gander at Utah’s Goosenecks

1.why: Gravitational potential energy depends directly on mass, gravity, and height.

wrong.a: Temperature does not determine potential energy.
wrong.c: Wind speed does not power the water flow here.
wrong.d: Air pressure does not directly equal Ep.

2.why: h stands for the vertical height or drop of the water.

3.why: Higher drops and heavier water streams give rivers more energy to carve rock.

wrong.a: Slower water has less kinetic and erosive energy.
wrong.b: Dry riverbeds lack water mass and flow.
wrong.d: Flat plains reduce water flow speed.

_quiz_pool.question: What does Ep stand for in Ep = m × g × h?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Ep is gravitational potential energy stored by height.

_quiz_pool.question: Which factor does NOT affect gravitational potential energy?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Color has no effect on gravitational energy.

_quiz_pool.question: What is the unit of gravitational potential energy Ep?
If you double the water mass, its potential energy…
_quiz_pool.explanation: Ep grows in direct proportion to mass m.

_quiz_pool.question: Why do rivers carve deep canyons when flowing from high plateaus?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Falling water converts potential energy into kinetic energy to erode rock.

_quiz_pool.question: In Ep = m × g × h, what is g?
_quiz_pool.explanation: g is acceleration due to gravity (approx 9.81 m/s²).

_quiz_pool.question: What is a river meander?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Meanders are winding loops carved by river flow.

_quiz_pool.question: 1 kJ is equal to how many joules?
Which value is standard for Earth gravity g in calculations?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Earth's gravitational acceleration is roughly 9.81 m/s².

_quiz_pool.question: What happens to potential energy when water flows down a 300 m canyon?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Height decreases, converting potential energy into motion and erosion.

must_show: a small tray or inclined board with sand or soil
pouring a cup of water down the incline
showing how flowing water cuts channels in the sand
safety: no flame, no hot water, no electricity
_lab_rubric.pass_if: The photos show water flowing down an inclined slope and carving channels in sand or soil.

cover.fun_fact: The San Juan River travels 5.5 miles between two points that are only 1.3 miles apart as the goose flies. [1]
story.title: The winding San Juan River
story.lead: Space station astronauts photographed the stunning, horseshoe-shaped meanders of the San Juan River in Utah [1]. Millions of years ago, tectonic forces lifted the plateau, speeding up the water [1].
story.image_caption: San Juan River meanders, photographed from the ISS on 6 October 2026 [1]
stat.1.label: depth of the canyon carved by the river
stat.2.label: Earth gravity acceleration in m/s² [4]
stat.3.label: potential energy of 1 ton of water at 300 m
story.body_1: Rivers shape the face of our planet by moving water and sediment across landscapes [2]. When tectonic uplift raises a region, rivers gain steepness and erosive power [1]. The water cuts downward through 300-million-year-old rock, forming deep canyons and dramatic meanders known as goosenecks [1].
story.body_2: Water is vital for ecosystems and climate worldwide [3]. Understanding how flowing water stores and releases energy helps scientists protect river basins and manage water resources safely [2].
timeline.1.text: The San Juan River flows across a relatively flat plain.
timeline.2.text: Tectonic forces uplift the Colorado Plateau, speeding up the river.
timeline.3.text: The river carves deep meanders into 300-million-year-old rock.
physics.title: Potential energy of water
physics.body_1: Water perched high on a plateau holds gravitational potential energy due to its height above sea level. When water flows downward, this stored energy converts into motion and erosion.
physics.body_2: The energy depends on three factors: mass, gravity, and height. More mass or a higher drop gives the river greater potential energy to carve stone.
physics.assumptions: Example masses, not measurements; use canyon depth as a drop; ignore friction. Gravity: 9.81 m/s² [4].
table.note: Potential energy increases directly with the mass of water.
